schema.description: A confirmation that the request succeeded.

message.description: What was done, written for people.

400.description: The password doesn't meet your organization's password policy. `errors.Password` names the rule it failed; `errors.IsPwned` is invalid when the password appears in a known data breach and your policy checks for that.

schema.title: Error
schema.description: Every error response has this shape. Match on `id`, which is stable, not on `message`, which may change.

id.description: A stable, machine-readable code for the error. Match on it to handle an error.

x-enumDescriptions.invalid_request_body: The request body failed validation. `errors` lists the rejected fields. Returned with `400`.
x-enumDescriptions.invalid_params: A required value is missing or empty. Returned with `422`.
x-enumDescriptions.forbidden: The request is authenticated but not allowed, for example because a plan limit is reached. Returned with `403`.
x-enumDescriptions.not_found: The object doesn't exist, or belongs to another organization. Returned with `404`.
x-enumDescriptions.unprocessable_entity: The request conflicts with the current state, for example a login name that's taken. Returned with `422`.
x-enumDescriptions.too_many_requests: The same action was requested too recently. Wait before retrying. Returned with `429`.
x-enumDescriptions.internal_server_error: Something failed on our side. Returned with `500`.

message.description: An explanation for people. Safe to log; don't show it to end users verbatim.

errors.description: The fields that were rejected, and why. Present only on `400` responses, either as an object keyed by field name or as a list of fields. Handle both.

oneOf.title: ValidationError
oneOf.description:
Field-level detail on a `400` caused by an invalid request body.

Each validated field appears as its own property, keyed by its name as sent; nested fields use
dotted paths such as `Settings.Network`. Fields that passed are listed too, with `isInvalid:
false`, so filter on `isInvalid` to find the failures.

isValid.description: Always `false` when this object is returned.

additionalProperties.description: The outcome for one field of the request body.

message.description: Why the field was rejected. Empty when the field passed.

UserName.message: Unfortunately, username can't be shorter than 5 characters.

items.title: FieldError
items.description: One field that was rejected, and why.

field.description: The name of the field, as it was sent.

message.description: Why the field was rejected, written for a person.
examples: Unfortunately, two virtual folders can't share the same path.

Password.message: Unfortunately, password can't be shorter than 30 characters and it must include a number and a lowercase letter.

401.description:
The request isn't authenticated.

The `Authorization` header is missing or malformed, the key is revoked, the key belongs to another organization than the one in the path, or the organization isn't active. The request is rejected before it reaches the endpoint, so the body has only `message`.

schema.title: AuthenticationError
schema.description: The body of a `401` returned before the request reaches the endpoint.

404.description: No such credentials, or they belong to another organization. The two cases look the same, so the existence of another organization's credentials can't be probed.

500.description:
Something failed on our side.

A change may or may not have been made, so retrieve the credentials before you retry one. Retrying
a read is always safe. If the error persists, contact support with the time of the request.
